newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end at new high, led by Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end at new high, led by Ericsson.

text.p: Swedish shares ended at a new high on Wednesday with market heavyweight Ericsson leading the rally while U.S. data and gains on bourses across Europe and in New York cheered the market.
The Stockholm general index rose 1.43 percent to 3,189.39 as some interest returned to the quiet summer market and shares worth 4.17 billion crowns changed hands.
"CPI levels and industrial production in the U.S. were positive and the U.S. bourse opened with gains," said one broker.
"It's mainly U.S. investors that are making things happen."
"I think Swedish fund buyers are just sitting on the sidelines watching the action."
Telecoms group Ericsson climbed 12 crowns to 340.5, buoyed by gains in U.S. high-tech stocks.
Salomon Brothers said it had started coverage of Ericsson with a buy recommendation but said it preferred Finnish rival Nokia Oy for a one-year investment.
Another market heavyweight, drugs company Astra, closed two higher at 157 crowns.
Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz rose up to 354.5 crowns but closed six higher at 337.
Positive industry sales figures pushed the price higher.
"People have been fascinated by the share for a while now and I believe it can continue to climb," one broker said.
Vehicle maker Volvo rose six crowns to 212 and industrial engineering company Atlas Copco rose seven to 235 which brokers saw as a recovery after falls last week.

Office supplier Esselte slipped two to 192 crowns. It posted a four percent rise in pre-tax profits for the first half of 1997 and said it expected to reach its company goal of an annual rise in pre-tax profits of 10 percent.
